title: Returning Goods
goal: Explain why you are returning an item, ask about a refund or exchange, and respond when the first option is unavailable.

runs.text: A
return
brings a purchased item back. A
refund
returns money. An
exchange
replaces the item with another one.
Store credit
is an amount available to spend with that store under its conditions. A
receipt
or
order number
helps identify a purchase, but acceptable proof and remedies depend on the actual seller and applicable rules.

study.title: Begin with the request and reason

runs.text: I'd like to return this jacket. It's too small
combines the request and explanation. Other reasons include
I bought the wrong size
It arrived damaged
The lamp doesn't turn on
, and
I received the wrong item
. Describe what happened; you do not need to diagnose an electrical fault to report it.
How can I help?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I'd like to return this jacket. It doesn't fit.

turns.en: I'd like to return this jacket. It doesn't fit.

runs.text: Do you have the receipt?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Yes. I bought it last week.

turns.en: Yes. I bought it last week.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Would you prefer an exchange or a refund?

turns.en: Would you prefer an exchange or a refund?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: An exchange, if you have a larger size.

turns.en: An exchange, if you have a larger size.

runs.text: I'll check that for you.

blocks.caption: Begin with the request and reason · Employee & Customer

runs.text: This is an original scene, not a statement about every store's policy.
Would you prefer...?
asks which option you want.
If you have...
makes the exchange depend on availability.

study.title: Practice with a complete fictional policy

runs.text: For the next scenes only, Elm Shop's policy says: unused clothing can be returned within 30 days with a receipt; refunds or exchanges are available; without a receipt, staff must review the purchase and cannot promise an outcome. The jacket was bought 10 days ago and has not been worn. This policy is a fictional exercise condition.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I'd like a refund for this jacket. Here's the receipt.

turns.en: I'd like a refund for this jacket. Here's the receipt.

runs.text: Thank you. Was it worn?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: No. I tried it on at home, but it was too small.

turns.en: No. I tried it on at home, but it was too small.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Under our policy, we can process the refund.

turns.en: Under our policy, we can process the refund.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Thanks. How will I receive it, and how long will it take?

turns.en: Thanks. How will I receive it, and how long will it take?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: I'll explain the details before we finish.

turns.en: I'll explain the details before we finish.

blocks.caption: Practice with a complete fictional policy · Customer & Employee

runs.text: Asking
How will I receive it?
avoids assuming a payment method.
How long will it take?
asks about timing without inventing a universal deadline.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I bought this online, but I can't find the receipt. I have the order number.

turns.en: I bought this online, but I can't find the receipt. I have the order number.

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: I can look up the order, but I need to check which options are available.

turns.en: I can look up the order, but I need to check which options are available.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Okay. I would prefer a refund. What information do you need?

turns.en: Okay. I would prefer a refund. What information do you need?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: The order number and the item, please.

turns.en: The order number and the item, please.

blocks.caption: When there is a problem · Customer & Employee

runs.text: If an offer does not meet your need, you can say
An exchange won't work for me. What other options are available?
A firmer response is
I'm frustrated because this arrived broken. I'd like you to review the return options.
It states the problem without inventing a right or accusing the staff member of causing it.
If the answer is
We can't decide that here
, ask
Who can review it?
or
Could you show me the policy you're referring to?
If you accept an alternative,
Store credit would work for me
makes that clear. You can also say
I need time to think about that
Speak both roles alone. Use Elm Shop's fictional conditions, not a real store's rules.
Return the unused jacket bought 10 days ago. You have the receipt and want an exchange. Ask whether a large is available.
The large is unavailable. The employee offers a refund. Accept it and ask about timing.
An online lamp arrived broken. You have the order number but no receipt. Explain the issue and ask what information is needed. Do not assume the outcome.
The employee offers only an exchange while reviewing the lamp's purchase. Explain that you prefer a refund and request a review.
Sample possibilities:

“I'd like to exchange this for a large. Here's my receipt.” / “A refund would be fine. How long will it take?” / “This lamp arrived broken. I have the order number. What information do you need?” / “An exchange won't work for me. Could someone review the refund options?”
Later, change the item and your preferred outcome. Check that you separated the reason for return, the remedy you want, and the seller's actual response. Several wordings can complete the task.

ja: 理由を伝え、返金か交換か。
note: 返したい品物、理由、希望する対応を分けます。この章の架空の返品条件を読み、使える選択肢を確認します。
